facts.fact: The Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy states that The Gambia signed the African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection at the African Union Commission in Addis Ababa on 2 December 2022, the Minister signing for the country and joining 14 other signatory states.

facts.fact: The Minister reiterated the Government's commitment to ratify the Convention after signature to pave the way for domestication; the statement reports no ratification (the AU Legal Counsel's deputy urged The Gambia to ratify, domesticate and implement it). The page carries no publication date, so the event date is used.

facts.fact: The African Union Commission's status list dated 2 February 2026 records The Gambia as having signed the Convention on 2 December 2022, with no date of ratification or accession and no date of deposit; the list counts 21 signatures and 20 deposits among 55 states.

facts.fact: The head of the Africa Fintech Network is quoted saying that a fintech licensed in Ghana wanting to enter The Gambia must start the licensing process afresh, as licence passporting across African markets is only a proposal under AUC and AfricaNenda harmonisation work (dated by the article's publication date, 7 October 2026).
The Minister says the Government of The Gambia ratified the AU Malabo Convention in March 2024.

note: Smart Africa membership is not a legal text signed or ratified.

facts.fact: Minister Ceesay told the Assembly that the Gambia is a signatory to the Africa Malabo Convention.
